explain.say: A car body holds several thousand spot welds; a ship hull, kilometres of arc weld. Welding joins metals by melting or softening them together into one piece. Look at the families, grouped by where the heat comes from: an electric arc, electrical resistance, friction, or a beam of light or electrons.

explain.say: Arc welding is the workhorse. In stick welding a flux-coated rod melts into the joint. In MIG a wire is fed automatically through a gun with shielding gas, fast and easy. In TIG a tungsten electrode makes the arc and filler is added by hand: slow, but very clean, ideal for thin stainless and aluminium. Which would you choose for a production line?

explain.say: MIG, or a robot doing MIG or spot welding! Spot welding clamps two sheets between copper electrodes and passes a huge current; resistance heat melts a small nugget. Friction stir welding never melts the metal at all: a spinning tool stirs soft metal together, great for aluminium. Now, how much heat does an arc put in?

explain.say: Heat input is efficiency times volts times amps over travel speed. A MIG arc at 25 volts and 200 amps, moving 5 millimetres per second, puts in 800 joules per millimetre. That heat shapes the weld. See the cross-section: the melted weld metal, the fusion line, then the heat-affected zone. Why might the heat-affected zone be weaker?

explain.say: It was heated but not melted, so its grains may have grown or hardened, and it is often where cracks start. Excellent. Real link: welders preheat thick steel to slow cooling and avoid hard, brittle zones. Exam tip: TIG gives the best quality, MIG the best speed, stick the most portable.

faq.q: What is the difference between MIG and TIG welding?
faq.a: MIG feeds a consumable wire electrode through the gun with shielding gas, so it is fast and easy. TIG uses a non-consumable tungsten electrode with separate filler, which is slower but gives cleaner, more precise welds.
Two sheets are clamped between copper electrodes and a very large current is passed for a fraction of a second. Resistance at the joint melts a small nugget that fuses the sheets.
The part of the joint that was melted, a mix of filler and base metal, which freezes into a cast structure.
The band of base metal next to the weld that was heated enough to change its grain structure and properties, but not melted. It can be harder, softer or more brittle than the parent metal.

faq.q: How do I calculate welding heat input?
faq.a: Heat input equals arc efficiency times voltage times current divided by travel speed, usually given in joules or kilojoules per millimetre.

facts: Friction stir welding was invented at TWI in the UK in 1991.
Resistance spot welding is the main joining method for steel car bodies.
